rules.summary: x op concat(y, c, z) with c in {0,1,~0} -> concat(x[..] op y, x[..] op c, x[..] op z)
rules.guard_comparison: C++ takes the first concat child and splits it at its first const (required to be 0/1/ones), with x = op of all other children in order. RARE pullup (const last) and pullup2 (const first) match directly. A middle const goes through the elaborator, which regroups the concat into (concat pre c post) (trust subgoal, re-proved) and then applies pullup3. The RARE rules are sound for any split, so the 0/1/ones restriction is only a heuristic. Probed each op at each position, multi-child prefix/suffix, n-ary x with the concat between other children, a 1-bit #b1 constant, two concat children (both with middle consts, and end-then-middle). Between the binary and HEAD the C++ is unchanged, but HEAD no longer runs FlattenAssocCommutNoDuplicates on and/or/xor (4e310090c3), so HEAD may see nested ops as x; RARE list patterns treat those as single elements.

rules.dispatch: BITVECTOR_MULT via RewriteMult, post-rewrite only, after FlattenAssocCommut and MultSimplify (src/theory/bv/theory_bv_rewriter.cpp:553)
rules.summary: x*...*(+/-2^k) -> concat((+/-x...)[w-k-1:0], 0_k); several pow2 consts sum exponents; exponent>=w -> 0
rules.guard_comparison: The RARE rules cover one +2^k or -2^k constant that follows at least one non-constant child. MultSimplify (which always runs first and returns if it changes the node) folds constants into a single constant at the end, drops 1, and turns ~0 into bvneg. So the C++ only sees one constant c, never 1 or ~0, in last position. The C++ multi-constant, children-empty and exponent>=w branches are therefore unreachable. Probed +4, the msb 8 (positive branch is chosen first, matching -1's int.ispow2), -4, -2, n-ary, n-ary negative, and x*2*2.
rules.probe_result: 8 probes: cvc5=unsat, no trust, rare=bv-mult-pow2-1/2; differential agrees; ethos correct
rules.rationale: Every reachable input form is one RARE instance. The unreachable C++ branches have no RARE counterpart, but dispatch never reaches them.

rules.dispatch: BITVECTOR_EXTRACT via RewriteExtract, 2nd in final LinearRewriteStrategy (src/theory/bv/theory_bv_rewriter.cpp:391); no ProofRewriteRule
rules.guard_comparison: The C++ requires both multiplicands to be BITVECTOR_CONCAT whose first child is a constant, and accepts any number of concat children. The RARE pattern is (concat (@bv x1i x1in) x2) with a single x2, so a 3+-child concat only matches binary concats. The leading-zero arithmetic agrees (int1.length() equals 1+log2), as do the k<=low boundary and the >64 guard. In the binary, the RARE rule lacks HEAD's (>= x1i 0)/(< x1i 2^x1in) guards (always true for constants).
